title: PGSB: Pretrained-Guided Shared Basis for LoRA Model Merging
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A two-stage procedure first extracts shared subspaces, then refines them against pretrained weights, enabling merging in a better-suited basis.
layout: 3 columns separated by dashed lines, left-to-right, stacked blocks with SVD arrows
description: A wide three-column diagram divided by dashed vertical lines. Column 1, 'Stage 1: Task-shared Subspace Extraction', shows T rounded boxes of LoRA updates ΔW_t, each holding trapezoid A and B factors. Arrows lead to concatenated ΔW rows and their transposes, then an SVD step down to U_L Σ_L V_L^T and U_R Σ_R V_R^T trapezoid blocks. Column 2, 'Stage 2: Pretrained-Coupled Coordinate Refinement', shows a box T containing Σ_L, U_L^T, the green W_0, U_R and Σ_R. An SVD step gives O_L Σ_T O_R^T, which splits into the bases Q_L=[U_L, O_L] and Q_R=[U_R, O_R]. Column 3, 'Merging and Reconstruction', has three stacked rows. Stacked task cards are projected into core matrices {C_t}, merged by M into C*, then added to W_0 to give W_merge. Pastel blue, green and lavender distinguish the matrix types.
caption: Overview of PGSB.Given task-specific LoRA updates, PGSB first performs Task-shared Subspace Extraction by decomposing the concatenated updates and their transposed counterparts, producing shared support matrices. PGSB then performs Pretrained-Coupled Coordinate Refinement, where the extracted supports are coupled with the pretrained weight geometry to obtain pretrained-compatible multi-task bases. Finally, task updates are projected into the refined bases, merged by a downstream merge operator M, and reconstructed back to the original parameter space to obtain the final merged model.
abstract: Large pretrained models have achieved remarkable success across diverse domains, yet adapting them to multiple downstream tasks remains challenging: full fine-tuning is costly, while maintaining separate task-specific models is storage-inefficient and fails to produce a unified multi-task model. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) offers an efficient alternative for Model Merging by representing each task adaptation as a low-rank update over frozen pretrained weights. However, existing LoRA merging methods often treat task-specific updates as directly comparable objects and merge them in their original low-rank parameter spaces. This overlooks two key factors: which update directions provide reliable shared support across tasks, and how these directions should be re-parameterized with respect to the pretrained weights before merging. To address this limitation, we propose Pretrained-Guided Shared Basis (PGSB), a two-stage framework for LoRA model merging. PGSB first identifies shared directions among task-specific LoRA updates, and then re-parameterizes these directions using their interaction with the pretrained weights, producing a more suitable basis for merging. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PGSB consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple benchmarks. Codes are available at https://github.com/Kitschnada/Pretrained-Basis .
